$comment: THE PHOTOGRAPHY MANIFEST.
Every photograph in the commercial surfaces is a named slot with its art
direction written down, so the picture is chosen against a brief rather
than because it was available. A slot with src:null renders as a reserved
plate carrying its own brief — visibly unfinished, which is the honest
state. Nothing here ever renders a fabricated image in a photograph's place.
FILLING A SLOT: put the file in /public/img/ and set src, credit, licence
and sourceUrl. The page needs no edit. scripts/photography-fetch.js pulls
candidates for a slot from a licensed library and writes them to
/public/img/candidates/<slot>/ for review; it never fills src by itself,
because the whole point is that a person rejects the clichés.
THE FILTER, applied to every candidate before it is accepted:
YES  real aestheticians · real consultation rooms · realistic clients ·
natural skin · believable ages · human expressions · hands, eye
contact, listening · warm premium clinic interiors · European where
possible · the photograph serves the story on the page
NO   obvious AI faces · futuristic clinics · doctors holding tablets ·
exaggerated luxury stock · plastic skin · fabricated before/after ·
corporate SaaS imagery · models who add no meaning · anything
implying a procedure MIRROR does not train

hero.role: The first thing a clinic owner sees. Must read as her own consultation room, not a brochure.
hero.brief: A practitioner mid-consultation, listening. She is not talking, not pointing at a mirror, not holding a tablet. The client's face may be turned away or out of frame — the subject is the act of attention. Warm interior, daylight, real clinic furniture.

carmen.role: Carmen's portrait, beside her own words. The single most important image in the product.
carmen.brief: A woman of about 51, composed and slightly guarded, seated. Natural skin with visible expression lines — the lines are the case. Not smiling for a camera. Not a beauty shot. She should look like a gallery director who reads contracts, because she is one.

coaching.role: Manager value. A clinic owner coaching one practitioner, not addressing a room.
coaching.brief: Two women at a table, one explaining, one listening and taking it in. Notebook or printed page between them. Back-of-house clinic setting, not a boardroom. Peer-to-peer posture, no lectern energy.

room.role: The consultation environment itself, as a breath between sections.
room.brief: Treatment-room or consultation-room detail with no people: two chairs at a slight angle to each other, a consultation form, a folded towel, daylight. Warm and real. Must not look like a hospital or a spa advertisement.

team.role: Five seats — the clinic team the licence covers.
team.brief: Three or four clinic staff of visibly different ages together, in work clothes, in their own space. Working, not posing in a line. One of them should look like she has been doing this for twenty years.

reception.role: The front of the funnel — where the consultation begins before anyone speaks.
reception.brief: Clinic reception or waiting area, warm and small rather than grand. A client waiting, or the desk itself. Believable for an independent clinic, not a chain.
